text: The back wheel had been rubbing against the frame for a week before I finally took the bicycle apart on the balcony. It turned out the axle nut on the left side had worked itself loose, so the whole wheel sat a few millimetres out of true. Tightening it took two minutes. Working out that this was what the noise meant took seven days.

We had four kilos of plums and no plan, so the afternoon went on jars. Stones out, sugar in, and then the long wait at the stove while the whole flat filled with steam. The first batch set too hard because I boiled it past the point I had been warned about. The second came out right, and there are eleven jars on the shelf now, enough to be giving away by March.

The storm came in from the west and arrived about two hours earlier than the forecast said it would. Power went out along our street just after seven and stayed out until the middle of the night. Nothing was damaged apart from one fence panel, but the whole neighbourhood spent the evening outside with torches, talking to people they had not spoken to in months.

The library has moved its reference section to the second floor, which nobody seems to have been told about. I spent twenty minutes looking for an atlas that had been reshelved three metres from where the catalogue said it was. The librarian was apologetic and clearly tired of explaining it. She said the move was finished in June and the catalogue is updated one section at a time.

The replacement bus took the long route through every village on the way, which turned a forty-minute train journey into an hour and fifty. Nobody complained. Two people slept, one read the whole way, and the driver announced each stop by name as though it were a tour. I arrived late for the meeting and it had been moved anyway.
